metadata.scope: e_andong (271 baronies across k_balhae, k_khitan, k_luzhen, k_raole)
metadata.hierarchy_note: hierarchy reflects data/ck3_title_tree.json (save-derived de jure tree including x_script_* dynamic titles); downstream localisation/historicity mods should key on barony_key and join against their target landed_titles tree.

schema_notes.modern_name: Clean modern/vanilla English display name of the audited settlement or holding.
schema_notes.hierarchy: De jure title hierarchy from data/ck3_title_tree.json (empire, kingdom, duchy, county, holding_type).
schema_notes.first_mention_year: Integer year of earliest documented attestation (negative values = BCE; null if no pre-modern attestation was identified).
schema_notes.first_mention_attestation: Summary of the earliest documented textual or epigraphic attestation (or unattested status).
schema_notes.is_historical_867: Boolean: true iff first_mention_year is known and <= 867 CE for the audited barony name.
schema_notes.named_after_post_867_person: Boolean: true if the title name incorporates a person, saint, or dynasty post-dating 867 CE.
schema_notes.eponym_details: Explanatory text for any eponymous origin (both pre-867 and post-867 eponyms); null if not eponymous or unrecorded.
schema_notes.natural_proper_name: Object indicating whether the title derives from a hydronym, oronym, choronym, or topographic_feature.
schema_notes.morphemes: List of constituent roots/morphemes with form, language, language_code (ISO 639-3 / ISO 639-5), and English translation.
schema_notes.etymology_analysis: Linguistic and historical etymology of the audited barony name.
schema_notes.older_name_by_867: Object indicating whether a distinct older name strictly attested <= 867 CE exists for the same site or immediate predecessor.
schema_notes.source_url: Primary reference URL (typically Wikipedia or regional historical encyclopedia), or null if unavailable.

b_Liao_Xijing.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Xijing (Western Capital, 西京) of Balhae's Yalu Province (鴨綠府) in Jia Dan's Huanghua Sida Ji (c. 785–805 CE), preserved in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Xijing.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 西京 (Xījīng, 'Western Capital'; Korean Seogyeong 서경), the designation of Balhae's western secondary capital at Shenzhou (神州) in Yalu Province (鴨綠府), located near modern Linjiang, Jilin.

b_Liao_Luzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Liao dynasty after conquering Balhae in 926 CE, renaming Balhae's Shenzhou (神州) of Xijing Yalu Province to Luzhou (渌州), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Luzhou2.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 渌州 (Lùzhōu), combining 渌 (clear green water, referencing the Yalu River) and 州 (prefecture), coined after 926 CE to replace Balhae's Shenzhou (神州).

names: Xijing Yalu Fu / Seogyeong Amnokbu (西京鴨綠府)
older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Jia Dan's Huanghua Sida Ji (c. 785–805 CE), quoted in Xin Tangshu (1060 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Before the Liao conquest of 926 CE, this site was Shenzhou (神州), the seat of Balhae's Western Capital Yalu Province (西京鴨綠府).

b_Liao_Fusong.first_mention_attestation: Fusong County (抚松县) was established in 1910 CE (Xuantong 2nd year of the Qing dynasty).
b_Liao_Fusong.etymology_analysis: Modern county name 抚松 (Fǔsōng), coined in 1910 CE with the auspicious meaning 'pacifying the Songhua River basin' (or 'soothing the pines').

b_FIC_Liao_Changbaishan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Changbaishan); no written attestation <= 867 CE as a settlement or administrative barony.
b_FIC_Liao_Changbaishan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding named after Changbai Mountain (长白山, 'Perpetually White Mountain', Korean Paektusan), the volcanic massif on the China–North Korea border.

b_FIC_Liao_Tianchi.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Tianchi); no written attestation <= 867 CE as a settlement or administrative barony.
b_FIC_Liao_Tianchi.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding named after Heaven Lake (天池, Tiānchí; Korean Cheonji), the crater lake atop Paektu/Changbai Mountain.

b_Liao_Changling.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Changling Fu (長嶺府 / Jangnyeongbu), one of the 15 provinces of Balhae established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Changling.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 長嶺 (Chánglǐng; Korean Jangnyeong 장령), 'Long Ridge', the name of Balhae's Changling Province (長嶺府) situated along the upper Songhua / Huifa River corridor.

b_FIC_Liao_Quliuan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Quliuan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Quliuan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 landscape compound 曲流岸 (Qūliú'àn, 'Winding-Flow Bank') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_FIC_Liao_Beichang.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Beichang); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Beichang.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 directional-auspicious compound 北昌 (Běichāng, 'North Prosperity') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Zhengzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Zhengzhou (正州 / Jeongju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Yalu Province (鴨綠府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Zhengzhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 正州 (Zhèngzhōu; Korean Jeongju 정주), a Balhae prefecture under Yalu Province located in the Fu'er River basin near modern Tonghua, Jilin.

b_Liao_Kuandianzi.first_mention_attestation: Founded in 1573 CE (Wanli 1st year of the Ming dynasty) as Kuandianbao (宽甸堡), one of the Kuandian Six Forts (宽甸六堡), and renamed Kuandian in 1877 CE.
b_Liao_Kuandianzi.etymology_analysis: From Ming-era frontier fort name 宽甸堡 (Kuāndiànbǎo, 'Broad Plain Fort', originally 宽奠堡), later colloquially 宽甸子 (Kuāndiànzi) and modern Kuandian Manchu Autonomous County, Liaoning.

b_Liao_Huanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Goguryeo's capital Hwando / Wan-du (丸都, later written 桓都) in the Sanguozhi (c. 280 CE), and established as Balhae's Huanzhou (桓州 / Hwanju) under Yalu Province by 830 CE (Xin Tangshu).
b_Liao_Huanzhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 桓州 (Huánzhōu; Korean Hwanju 환주), named after its seat at Huandu County (桓都縣, modern Ji'an, Jilin), the former Goguryeo capital of Hwando/Gungnae.

b_FIC_Liao_Yaluan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Yaluan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Yaluan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 locator compound 雅鲁岸 (Yǎlǔ'àn, 'Yalu Bank') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Hezhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Hezhou (河州 / Haju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Changling Province (長嶺府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Hezhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 河州 (Hézhōu; Korean Haju 하주), 'River Prefecture', a Balhae prefecture under Changling Province seated near Shancheng Town, Meihekou, Jilin.

b_FIC_Liao_Hongfucun.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Hongfucun); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Hongfucun.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 auspicious village name 洪福村 (Hóngfúcūn, 'Great Fortune Village') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_FIC_Liao_Baichang.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Baichang); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Baichang.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 auspicious compound 百昌 (Bǎichāng, 'Hundredfold Prosperity') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Changchun2.first_mention_attestation: Established as Changchun Prefecture (長春州) by the Liao dynasty in 1039 CE (Chongxi 8th year), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Changchun2.etymology_analysis: From Liao-dynasty Changchun Prefecture (長春州, 'Perpetual Spring'), named after the Liao imperial spring hunting grounds (Chunshui / Changchun River) in western Jilin.

b_Liao_Weizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established under Liao's Huanglong Prefecture (黃龍府) in 1020 CE (Kaitai 9th year) as Weizhou Wuning Jun (威州武寧軍), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Weizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 威州 (Wēizhōu, 'Majesty Prefecture'), subordinate to Huanglong Fu, conquered by the Jurchen Jin in 1114 CE.

b_Liao_Binzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Liao dynasty in 999 CE (Tonghe 17th year) when Liao settled Wushe households at Binzhou (賓州), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Binzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 賓州 (Bīnzhōu, 'Guest/Submission Prefecture'), located at Guangyuandian in modern Nong'an County, Jilin.

b_Liao_Xiangzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Liao Emperor Xingzong (r. 1031–1055 CE) using Tieli households and attested by 1053 CE in the Xu Zizhi Tongjian Changbian, as well as the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Xiangzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 祥州 (Xiángzhōu, 'Auspicious Prefecture'), located at Wanjinta in modern Nong'an County, Jilin.

b_Liao_Fuzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Fuzhou (扶州 / Buju), the capital prefecture of Balhae's Buyeo Province (夫餘府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Fuzhou2.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 扶州 (Fúzhōu; Korean Buju 부주), abbreviated from 夫餘 (Buyeo/Fuyu), the capital prefecture of Balhae's Buyeo Province.

b_Liao_Suzhou.first_mention_attestation: Liao-dynasty Suzhou (肅州, Xinling Jun), restored in 1041 CE (Chongxi 10th year) after its inhabitants fled to the Jurchens, recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Suzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 肅州 (Sùzhōu) in Dongjing Circuit, subordinate militarily to the Northern Jurchen Military Commissioner.

b_Liao_Tonghua.first_mention_attestation: Tonghua County (通化县) was established in 1877 CE (Guangxu 3rd year of the Qing dynasty).
b_Liao_Tonghua.etymology_analysis: Qing-era county name 通化 (Tōnghuà), coined in 1877 CE with the meaning 'open to civilizing influence'.

b_Liao_Xianzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Xianzhou (仙州 / Seonju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Buyeo Province (夫餘府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Xianzhou2.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 仙州 (Xiānzhōu; Korean Seonju 선주), a Balhae prefecture under Buyeo Province seated at Chengzishan Mountain City in Xifeng County, Liaoning.

b_Liao_Xinzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Liao Emperor Shengzong in the early Kaitai era (c. 1012 CE) on the former site of Balhae's Huaiyuan Fu (懷遠府) and ancient Yuexi (越喜), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Xinzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 信州 (Xìnzhōu, 'Fidelity Prefecture'), established at modern Qinjiatun Ancient City in Gongzhuling, Jilin.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (1060 CE) recording Balhae's 15 provinces by King Xuan's reign (818–830 CE); Liao Shi (1344 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi juan 38 states Xinzhou was built on the old city of Yuexi (越喜) where Balhae had previously established Huaiyuan Province (懷遠府).

b_FIC_Liao_Fuyunan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Fuyunan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Fuyunan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 frontier-bank compound 抚远岸 (Fǔyuǎn'àn, 'Pacify-Distant Bank') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Yizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established under Liao's Huanglong Prefecture (黃龍府) in 1020 CE (Kaitai 9th year) as an observation prefecture (益州觀察), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Yizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 益州 (Yìzhōu) subordinate to Huanglong Fu in Jilin (distinct from Balhae's Yizhou in Shuaibin Province).

b_Liao_Fengzhou3.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao-dynasty prefecture (鳳州, c. 10th–11th century) on former Gaoli and Balhae Anning Commandery territory, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Fengzhou3.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 鳳州 (Fèngzhōu, 'Phoenix Prefecture') in Shangjing Circuit, established on former Balhae territory.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Liao Shi (1344 CE, juan 37), citing Balhae's Anning Commandery (<= 867 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi juan 37 states that Liao's Fengzhou lay in the former territory of Gaoli and Balhae's Anning Commandery.

b_Liao_Jizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Jizhou (薊州) in 730 CE (Kaiyuan 18th year of the Tang dynasty), recorded in the Jiu Tangshu (945 CE) and Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Jizhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 薊州 (Jìzhōu), established by the Tang dynasty in 730 CE (named after the ancient Ji region) and later incorporated into Liao's Sixteen Prefectures.

b_Liao_Mozhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Mozhou (鄚州 / Makju), the capital prefecture of Balhae's Makhil Province (鄚頡府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Mozhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 鄚州 (Mòzhōu; Korean Makju 막주), the capital prefecture of Balhae's Makhil Province located in modern Acheng District, Harbin.

b_Liao_Gaozhou2.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Gaozhou (高州 / Goju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Makhil Province (鄚頡府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Gaozhou2.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 高州 (Gāozhōu; Korean Goju 고주), 'High Prefecture', a Balhae prefecture under Makhil Province located in modern Bin County, Heilongjiang.

b_FIC_Liao_Nanmoan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Nanmoan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Nanmoan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 directional compound 南漠安 (Nánmò'ān, 'South Desert Peace') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_FIC_Liao_Longfengshan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Longfengshan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Longfengshan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 auspicious oronym 龙凤山 (Lóngfèngshān, 'Dragon-Phoenix Mountain') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Suzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Suzhou (涑州 / Sokju), a direct-control prefecture (獨奏州) of Balhae established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Suzhou2.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 涑州 (Sùzhōu; Korean Sokju 속주), a Balhae direct-control prefecture named after the Sumo (Songhua) River, seated at Tuchengzi near modern Jilin City.

b_FIC_Liao_Suping.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Suping); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Suping.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 name 苏平 (Sūpíng) invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Yongji.first_mention_attestation: Yongji Prefecture (永吉州) was established in 1726 CE (Yongzheng 4th year of the Qing dynasty) within the Jilin Ula jurisdiction.
b_Liao_Yongji.etymology_analysis: Qing-era administrative name 永吉 (Yǒngjí, 'Eternally Auspicious'), first established as Yongji Zhou in 1726 CE and now Yongji County, Jilin.

b_Liao_Ningjiang.first_mention_attestation: Established as Ningjiang Prefecture (寧江州, Huntong Jun) by the Liao dynasty during the Qingning era (1055–1064 CE), recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE).
b_Liao_Ningjiang.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture name 寧江州 (Níngjiāngzhōu, 'Tranquil River Prefecture'), located at Shitouchengzi in Fuyu, Jilin, where the Jin–Liao War began in 1114 CE.

b_FIC_Liao_Moedu.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Moedu); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Moedu.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 compound 漠都 (Mòdū, 'Steppe Capital') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_FIC_Liao_Ximoan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Ximoan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Ximoan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 directional compound 西漠安 (Xīmò'ān, 'West Desert Peace') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Tongzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Tongzhou (銅州), a prefecture established by Balhae (<= 867 CE), as explicitly recorded in the Liao Shi (1344 CE, juan 38: '銅州，廣利軍，刺史。渤海置。').
b_Liao_Tongzhou2.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 銅州 (Tóngzhōu, 'Copper Prefecture'), established by Balhae in Liaodong near modern Ximu Town, Haicheng, Liaoning.

b_FIC_Liao_Tongan.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Tongan); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_FIC_Liao_Tongan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 auspicious compound 同安 (Tóng'ān, 'Harmonious Peace') invented to populate the CK3 map.

b_Liao_Sushen.first_mention_attestation: The Sushen (肅慎) people/polity are attested in the Shiji (-91 BCE), and Sushen County (肅慎縣) was established under Balhae's Longzhou (龍州) in Longquan Province by 830 CE (Xin Tangshu).
b_Liao_Sushen.etymology_analysis: From Old Chinese 肅慎 (Sùshèn), an ancient ethnonym for Tungusic peoples of Manchuria, later adopted by Balhae as the name of Sushen County (肅慎縣) under its Supreme Capital Longquan Fu.

b_FIC_Liao_Helong.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Helong); no written attestation <= 867 CE for this barony name.
b_FIC_Liao_Helong.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 barony using the modern city name Helong (和龙, 'Harmonious Dragon'), a county-level city in Yanbian, Jilin.

b_Liao_Xingzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Xingzhou (興州 / Heungju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Xiande Province (顯德府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Xingzhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 興州 (Xīngzhōu; Korean Heungju 흥주), 'Prospering Prefecture', a Balhae prefecture under Xiande Province.

b_FIC_Liao_Yanji.first_mention_attestation: Synthetic CK3 barony key (b_FIC_Liao_Yanji); no written attestation <= 867 CE for this barony name.
b_FIC_Liao_Yanji.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 barony using the modern city name Yanji (延吉, 'Enduring Auspiciousness'), the capital of Yanbian Korean Autonomous Prefecture, Jilin.

b_Liao_Luzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Luzhou (盧州 / Noju), a subordinate prefecture of Balhae's Xiande Province (顯德府) established by the reign of King Xuan (818–830 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Luzhou.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 盧州 (Lúzhōu; Korean Noju 노주), a Balhae prefecture under Xiande Province located in modern Antu County, Jilin, famous for Lucheng rice.

b_Liao_Zhongjing.first_mention_attestation: Attested as Zhongjing Xiande Fu (中京顯德府), Balhae's Central Capital under King Mun (who moved the royal court from Zhongjing to Shangjing c. 755 CE), recorded in the Xin Tangshu (1060 CE).
b_Liao_Zhongjing.etymology_analysis: From Classical Chinese 中京 (Zhōngjīng; Korean Junggyeong 중경), 'Central Capital', the designation of Balhae's Xiande Province (顯德府) at Xigucheng in Helong, Jilin.

b_Liao_Tangzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Balhae Kingdom by 830 CE under King Xuan (Dae Insu) as one of the six prefectures of Central Capital Xiande-fu, recorded in the Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Tangzhou2.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym meaning 'Hot-Spring Prefecture', coined by Balhae for its thermal springs on former Han Xiangping territory.

b_FIC_Liao_Nansuan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding name.
b_FIC_Liao_Nansuan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 Chinese-calqued compound ('South Reckoning') with no attested historical settlement.

b_FIC_Liao_Erdaojiang.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding named after the modern Erdaojiang River/District.
b_FIC_Liao_Erdaojiang.etymology_analysis: Chinese hydronym ('Second-Channel River'), referring to the Erdao River in Tonghua, Jilin.

b_Liao_Yingzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Balhae Kingdom by 830 CE as one of the three direct-report prefectures (duzhouzhou) alongside Tongzhou and Suzhou, recorded in Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Yingzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym borrowing the classical Chu capital name Ying plus 'prefecture', established by Balhae.

b_FIC_Liao_Yingan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding name.
b_FIC_Liao_Yingan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 Chinese auspicious compound ('Heroic Peace') with no attested historical settlement.

b_Liao_Shangjing.first_mention_attestation: Established in 756 CE (late Tianbao era) as Shangjing Longquanfu, the Upper Capital of Balhae under King Mun (Dae Heummu), recorded in Xin Tangshu (juan 219).
b_Liao_Shangjing.etymology_analysis: Chinese imperial capital designation ('Upper Capital'), modeled on Tang Chang'an as the primary capital of Balhae.

b_Liao_Bozhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Balhae Kingdom by 830 CE as one of the three prefectures under Upper Capital Longquan-fu, recorded in Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Bozhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Bo Prefecture') named after the Balhae (Bohai) state, subordinated to Longquan-fu.

b_FIC_Liao_Daguokuishan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding named after Mount Daguokui in the Zhangguangcai Range.
b_FIC_Liao_Daguokuishan.etymology_analysis: Chinese oronym ('Great Cauldron-Helmet Mountain') describing the helmet-shaped summit of the main peak at Yabuli in Heilongjiang.

b_FIC_Liao_Mudanjiang.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE under the name Mudanjiang; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding named after the Mudan River (historically Huhan / Hurka River).
b_FIC_Liao_Mudanjiang.etymology_analysis: Chinese hydronym ('Peony River'), a folk-etymological sinicization of Manchu Mudan ula ('winding river').

b_FIC_Liao_Qingquan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding name.
b_FIC_Liao_Qingquan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 generic Chinese landscape phrase ('Clear Spring') with no attested historical settlement.

b_Liao_Diezhou.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE in Liaodong/Andong; no Liao prefecture named Diezhou appears in Liao Shi (juan 38) or Xin Tangshu (juan 219).
b_Liao_Diezhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Layered-Terrace Prefecture'), misplaced or borrowed in CK3 from the historical Diezhou in Gansu with no Liaodong attestation.

b_Liao_Tongzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by the Balhae Kingdom by 830 CE as one of the three direct-report prefectures (duzhouzhou), recorded in Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Tongzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Copper Prefecture'), named for local copper-producing areas under Balhae.

b_Liao_Kaizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Kaizhou (Kaifeng-fu Kaiyuan-jun) by Liao Shengzong in 1014 CE (Kaitai 3), recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Kaizhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Opening Prefecture') coined by the Liao dynasty in 1014 CE.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) identifies Kaizhou as former Goguryeo Gyeongju (慶州) and Balhae Eastern Capital Longyuanfu (東京龍原府, also called Chakseongbu), where King Mun moved the Balhae capital in 785 CE.

b_Liao_Dandong.first_mention_attestation: The name Dandong ('Red East') was adopted on January 20, 1965, replacing Qing-era Andong (established 1876 CE).
b_Liao_Dandong.etymology_analysis: Modern Chinese toponym ('Red East') adopted in 1965 to replace Andong ('Pacifying the East').

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (111 CE) and Xin Tangshu (juan 43B, Jia Dan's Daoliji)
older_name_by_867.notes: Han-era Xi'anping County of Liaodong Commandery (Hanshu, 111 CE) and Goguryeo/Tang Bakjak Fortress (Bozhuo, Xin Tangshu) stood in the immediate Dandong area along the lower Yalu River.

b_Liao_Guidezhou.first_mention_attestation: Founded under Liao Taizong (r. 927–947 CE) by Yelü Chage and later named Guidezhou ('Virtue-Exalting Prefecture') by Liao Shengzong, recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Guidezhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Virtue-Exalting Prefecture') coined under the Liao dynasty.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Shiji (-91 BCE) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) records Guidezhou as former Han Xiangping territory (-91 BCE, Shiji) and Balhae Chongshan County (崇山縣, <= 867 CE).

b_Liao_Xiyuan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; not recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38) or Xin Tangshu (juan 219).
b_Liao_Xiyuan.etymology_analysis: Generic Chinese directional compound ('West Source') with no attested pre-867 settlement in Liaodong.

b_Liao_Fengcheng.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE in Liaodong; not recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38) or Xin Tangshu (juan 219).
b_Liao_Fengcheng.etymology_analysis: Chinese toponym ('Abundant Walled City'), unattested in Liaodong in Liao or pre-867 sources.

b_FIC_Liao_Shaozijiang.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 b_FIC_* holding name.
b_FIC_Liao_Shaozijiang.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 Chinese river-name compound ('Shaozi River') with no attested historical settlement.

b_Liao_Shenyang.first_mention_attestation: The name Shenyang (瀋陽路, 'north of the Shen River') was established in 1296 CE during the Yuan dynasty.
b_Liao_Shenyang.etymology_analysis: Chinese toponym meaning 'North (Sunny) Bank of the Shen River', coined in 1296 CE from earlier Shenzhou.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (111 CE) and Xin Tangshu (juan 219) / Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Han-era Houcheng County (Hanshu, 111 CE) stood at the Shenyang site, and Balhae later established Shenzhou (瀋州, <= 867 CE) under Dingli-fu.

b_Liao_Tangzhou.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE in Liaodong; Liao Shi (juan 38) records Tangzhou with 'hot spring' (湯州, audited as b_Liao_Tangzhou2), not 'Tang' (唐州).
b_Liao_Tangzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Tang Prefecture'), apparently a homophonic duplicate/misattribution in CK3 of Liaodong's 湯州 (Hot-Spring Prefecture).

b_Liao_Liaoyang.first_mention_attestation: The Liao dynasty renamed its Eastern Capital to Liaoyang-fu (遼陽府) in 938 CE (Tianxian 13), recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Liaoyang.etymology_analysis: Chinese toponym ('North Bank of the Liao River'), applied to the city as Liaoyang-fu by the Liao dynasty in 938 CE.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Shiji (-91 BCE) and Hanshu (111 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Continuously attested from Warring States Yan / Han Xiangping (-91 BCE, Shiji), Goguryeo Liaodongcheng, and Tang Andong Protectorate (668 CE).

b_Liao_Haizhou.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Haizhou (Nanhai-jun) by the Liao dynasty after conquering Balhae in 926 CE, recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Haizhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Sea Prefecture'), coined by the Liao dynasty from Balhae's Nanhai-fu ('Southern Sea Capital').

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) notes the site was Goguryeo's Sabi-seong (attacked by Tang Li Shiji in 645 CE) and Balhae's Southern Capital Nanhai-fu (<= 830 CE).

b_Liao_Yaozhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Yaozhou by the Liao dynasty after conquering Balhae in 926 CE, replacing Balhae's Jiaozhou, recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Yaozhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Brilliance Prefecture') coined by the Liao dynasty to replace Balhae Jiaozhou.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) explicitly states Yaozhou was formerly Balhae's Jiaozhou (椒州), one of the three prefectures under Nanhai-fu (Xin Tangshu, <= 830 CE).

b_Liao_Yinzhou.first_mention_attestation: Renamed Yinzhou (Fuguo-jun) by Liao Taizu (Yelü Abaoji) after conquering Balhae in 926 CE, recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Yinzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Silver Prefecture'), renamed by Liao Taizu from Balhae's Fuzhou due to silver smelting.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) states Yinzhou was formerly Balhae's Fuzhou (富州), a prefecture under Huaiyuan-fu in Xin Tangshu (<= 830 CE).

b_Liao_Qizhou.first_mention_attestation: Founded by Liao Taizu (after 926 CE) initially as Tanzhou and later renamed Qizhou (Yousheng-jun), recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Qizhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Fortunate Prefecture') coined by the Liao dynasty.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Xin Tangshu (juan 219) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) states Qizhou was built on former Balhae Mengzhou (蒙州) territory, attested under Dongping-fu in Xin Tangshu (<= 830 CE).

b_Liao_Guangzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Guangzhou in 1018 CE (Kaitai 7) by Liao Shengzong, recorded in Liao Shi (juan 38).
b_Liao_Guangzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('Vast Prefecture') established in 1018 CE by the Liao dynasty.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Shiji (-91 BCE) and Liao Shi (juan 38)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 38) records the site as former Han Xiangping territory (-91 BCE, Shiji), Goguryeo Dangshan County, and Balhae Tieli-jun (<= 830 CE).

b_Liao_Zhenzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative toponym ('True Prefecture'), unattested in Liaodong in Liao or pre-867 sources.

b_FIC_Liao_Biliujiang.etymology_analysis: Chinese hydronym ('Emerald-Flowing River'), referring to the Biliu River (Biliuhe) in southern Liaoning.

b_FIC_Amur_Yemantudi.etymology_analysis: Synthetic unoccupied CK3 barony key meaning 'Wild Land' in Mandarin Chinese, with no historical attestation.

b_FIC_Amur_Yerencao.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 compound meaning 'Wilderness People Grass' (calqued in-repo as Feltmanwêde), echoing Ming-Qing exonyms (Yeren Jurchens) and not attested as a settlement.

b_Amur_Suihua.first_mention_attestation: Established in 1885 CE (11th year of the Guangxu era, Qing dynasty) as Suihua Direct Subprefecture (绥化直隶厅 / 绥化理事通判厅), renamed from the Qing settlement Beituanlinzi (北团林子); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Amur_Suihua.etymology_analysis: Auspicious Qing administrative name meaning 'Pacify and Civilize' (calqued in-repo as StillKeêre), bestowed in 1885 CE when Beituanlinzi was elevated to Suihua Subprefecture.

b_FIC_Liao_Hongdali.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Hongdali.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 compound prefixing Mandarin 'red' (红) to 'Dali' (达里, from Dalai Nur), mis-calqued in-repo as RôtRêkdorp.

b_FIC_Liao_Matudi.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.

b_FIC_Liao_Caoyuanan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Caoyuanan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic unoccupied CK3 barony key meaning 'Steppe Peace', with no historical attestation.

b_Liao_Linhuang.first_mention_attestation: Founded in 918 CE (Shence 3rd year) by Liao Emperor Taizu (Yelü Abaoji) as Huangdu ('Imperial Capital') and renamed Shangjing Linhuangfu in 938 CE, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Linhuang.etymology_analysis: Locator compound meaning 'Overlooking the Huang River' (calqued in-repo as BîdemHuangflôz), referring to the Shira Muren (Xar Moron) River near the Liao Supreme Capital in Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia.

b_Liao_Huaizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established in 947 CE (Datong 1st year) by Emperor Shizong of Liao to tend Huailing, the mausoleum of Emperor Taizong, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no attestation as Huaizhou <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Huaizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture named after Huailing (怀陵, the mausoleum of Liao Taizong), meaning 'Cherish Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Koestergouwe). Liao Shi notes it occupied the site of Tang's Guichengzhou (归诚州).

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Old Book of Tang (Jiu Tang Shu, juan 199b) and New Book of Tang (Xin Tang Shu, juan 4 & 219), attesting Sun Wanrong as Prefect of Guichengzhou in the early Chuigong era (c. 685 CE) and 696 CE; identified as Huaizhou's predecessor in Liao Shi (juan 37).
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 37) states '本唐归诚州' ('originally Tang's Guicheng Prefecture').

b_Liao_Songzhanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37, compiled 1344 CE) as a Liao touxia military prefecture established in the Kaitai era (1012–1021 CE) on the grazing lands of Prince Pugu; no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Songzhanzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao touxia prefecture named after Mount Songshan ('Pine Mountain'), calqued in-repo as Pînberchgouwe.

b_Liao_Zuzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Emperor Taizong of Liao during the Tianxian era (926–938 CE, following Abaoji's burial at Zuling in 927 CE), as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Zuzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture meaning 'Ancestor Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Ahnengouwe), built around the mausoleum (Zuling) of Liao founder Yelü Abaoji in Bairin Left Banner, Inner Mongolia.

b_Liao_Yungzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established in 981 CE (Qianheng 3rd year) by Empress Dowager Chengtian beside the tomb of Prince Hanba at the confluence of the Huang and Tu rivers, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Yungzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture meaning 'Eternal Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Ewichgouwe), founded near sacred Mount Muye at the confluence of the Shira Muren (Huang) and Laoha (Tu) rivers.

b_Liao_Longhuazhou.first_mention_attestation: Built as a walled city in 902 CE (Tang Tianfu 2nd year) by Yelü Abaoji as yilijin of the Diela tribe, later serving as his Eastern Tower (Donglou), as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Longhuazhou.etymology_analysis: Early Khitan/Liao prefecture meaning 'Dragon Transformation Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as DrachenKeêregouwe), located in present-day Kailu County, Inner Mongolia.

b_Liao_Jiangshengzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Emperor Muzong of Liao (r. 951–969 CE) at the East Tower site where Emperor Taizong was born, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Jiangshengzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture meaning 'Descent of the Sage Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as HuldeHiliggouwe), commemorating the birth legend of Emperor Taizong at Aohan Banner, Inner Mongolia.

b_FIC_Liao_Huopingan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Huopingan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 compound meaning 'Fire Peace' (calqued in-repo as VûerEbeneFrid), with no historical attestation.

b_Liao_Raozhou.first_mention_attestation: Established under Liao Emperor Taizu (r. 907–926 CE; subordinate counties Linhe and Anmin set up in 926 CE) by repairing older fortifications in the former Tang Raole Prefecture, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no attestation as Raozhou <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Raozhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture meaning 'Abundant Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Rîchdomgouwe), shortened from the Tang-era Raole Area Command (饶乐府 / 饶乐都督府).

names: Raole Area Command (饶乐都督府 / 饶乐府)
older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Old Book of Tang and New Book of Tang, recording the establishment of Raole Area Command (饶乐都督府) in 648 CE (Zhen'guan 22nd year) for the Kumo Xi; cited as Raozhou's predecessor in Liao Shi (juan 37).
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 37) states '本唐饶乐府地' ('originally the territory of Tang's Raole Prefecture').

b_Liao_Qingzhou.first_mention_attestation: First built by Emperor Muzong (r. 951–969 CE) as Heihezhou, abolished in 990 CE, renamed Qingzhou by Emperor Shengzong, and formally re-established in 1031 CE (Jingfu 1st year), as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Qingzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture meaning 'Celebration Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Fröudegouwe), located in Bairin Right Banner, Inner Mongolia, near the Qingling imperial tombs.

b_FIC_Liao_Xilin.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Xilin.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key from Mongolic sili ('tableland/plateau', as in Xilingol, Sinicized as 锡林; mis-calqued character-by-character in-repo as Zinwalt 'Tin Forest').

b_FIC_Liao_Ulanulagai.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Ulanulagai.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key combining Mongolic ulaan ('red') and Ulagai (river name in Inner Mongolia), rendered in Chinese characters as 忽剌安兀鲁回 and mis-calqued in-repo as HûLâFridÔtLûHôei.

b_FIC_Liao_Ulanuer.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.

No written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Changchun.etymology_analysis: Auspicious Chinese name meaning 'Long Spring' (calqued in-repo as LangLentz), first used for Liao's Changchunzhou (1039 CE, near modern Qian'an, Jilin) and later for modern Changchun (1800 CE).

b_FIC_Liao_Yumitudi.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.

b_FIC_Liao_Heihorqin.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) combining Chinese 'black' with the post-867 Mongolic ethnonym Horqin (Khorchin).
b_FIC_Liao_Heihorqin.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 compound prefixing Mandarin 'black' (黑) to Mongolic Khorchin ('quiver-bearer'), mis-calqued character-by-character in-repo as SwartzVûerkenRôtInneem.

b_FIC_Liao_Shuangliao.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) borrowing the modern 20th-century name Shuangliao (established 1940).
b_FIC_Liao_Shuangliao.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key borrowing the modern city name Shuangliao ('Twin Liao', calqued in-repo as TwêLjô), formed in 1940 from Shuangshan and Liaoyuan.

b_FIC_Liao_Horqin.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) derived from the Mongolic ethnonym Khorchin.
b_FIC_Liao_Horqin.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key from Mongolic Khorchin ('quiver-bearer', an imperial guard title and later Mongol tribe), mis-calqued character-by-character in-repo as VûerkenRôtInneem.

b_FIC_Liao_Bayintailai.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Bayintailai.etymology_analysis: Synthetic unoccupied CK3 barony key from Mongolic bayan ('rich') + tala ('plain/steppe'), with no historical attestation.

b_FIC_Liao_Zhanyu.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Liao_Zhanyu.etymology_analysis: Synthetic unoccupied CK3 barony key (echoing modern Zhanyu Town in Tongyu County, Jilin), with no historical attestation <= 867 CE.

b_Liao_Ningzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao touxia military prefecture (c. 10th–11th century) on the grazing lands of Prince Guanning, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Ningzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao touxia prefecture meaning 'Tranquil Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Rûwegouwe), located in the grazing lands of Prince Guanning near Mount Lede.

b_Liao_Fengzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao touxia military prefecture (c. 10th–11th century) 350 li north of Shangjing on the former grazing lands of Yaonian Sengyin, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Fengzhou2.etymology_analysis: Liao touxia prefecture meaning 'Abundant Prefecture' in Shangjing Circuit, distinct from the western Fengzhou near Hohhot.

b_Liao_Taonan.first_mention_attestation: Established in 1904 CE (late Qing dynasty) as Taonan Fu (洮南府) following the 1902 opening of Khorchin Mongol lands to settlement; no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Taonan.etymology_analysis: Late-Qing directional/locator compound meaning 'South of the Tao'er River', in northwestern Jilin.

b_Liao_Chunzhou.first_mention_attestation: Abbreviated name of Changchunzhou (长春州), established in 1039 CE (Chongxi 8th year) by Emperor Xingzong of Liao, as recorded in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Chunzhou.etymology_analysis: Abbreviated Liao prefecture name ('Spring Prefecture') for Changchunzhou in western Jilin.

b_Amur_Taizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established during the Liao dynasty (under Emperor Xingzong, r. 1031–1055 CE) to relocate Tonghuazhou, and attested in the History of Liao (Liao Shi, juan 37, compiled 1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Amur_Taizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao frontier prefecture meaning 'Supreme Peace Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Grôzfridgouwe), located near modern Tailai County, Heilongjiang.

b_FIC_Amur_Jianali.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Amur_Jianali.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key (rendered as 假那礼 and calqued in-repo as LêhenNâSêde), with no historical attestation.

b_FIC_Amur_Nalidu.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources.
b_FIC_Amur_Nalidu.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key (rendered as 乃力度 and calqued in-repo as NaiKraftvurt), with no historical attestation.

b_FIC_Amur_Hongan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic CK3 holding name (`b_FIC_*`) not attested in historical sources in this region.
b_FIC_Amur_Hongan.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 holding key meaning 'Red Peace' (calqued in-repo as RôtFrid), with no historical attestation in the Amur/Liao region.

b_Liao_Wuzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao touxia prefecture (c. 10th–11th century) by Northern Great King Bola on former Wuhuan territory, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).

b_Liao_Wuzhou2.etymology_analysis: Liao prefecture named after the Wuhuan (乌丸) ethnonym (mis-calqued in-repo as Swartzgouwe 'Raven Prefecture').

b_Liao_Weizhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established in the early 11th century (c. 1016 CE) by Prince Consort Xiao Changyi with dowry households of Princess Hanguo (daughter of Yelü Longqing, d. 1016 CE), as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Weizhou2.etymology_analysis: Liao touxia prefecture borrowing the classical Chinese prefectural name Weizhou (calqued in-repo as Wêigouwe), located in modern Faku County, Liaoning.

b_Liao_Fuzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao touxia prefecture (c. 10th–11th century) by Imperial Uncle Xiao Ning using captured Han households, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Fuzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao touxia prefecture meaning 'Blessed Prefecture' (calqued in-repo as Sêlichgouwe), located east of Horqin Left Rear Banner, Inner Mongolia.

b_Liao_Yuanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Founded in the Liao dynasty (c. 10th–11th century) by maternal-uncle (guojiu) Jinde northeast of Xianzhou, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Yuanzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Plain Prefecture' (原州), established as a Liao dynasty touxia (appanage) military prefecture (头下军州) by Guojiu Jinde on former Han-era Bei'anping County territory.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 37) states Yuanzhou was built on the former territory of Han dynasty Bei'anping County (北安平县) of Liaodong Commandery.

b_Liao_Yizhou2.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 37–38, 1344 CE): established in Taiping 3 (1023 CE) by Princess Yueguo/Yanguo (daughter of Liao Shengzong) using her dowry retainer households (媵臣户).
b_Liao_Yizhou2.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Virtuous Prefecture' (懿州), an honorific name appropriate to a Liao princess's appanage prefecture (头下军州) founded in 1023 CE.

b_Liao_Dading.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): walled and established in Tonghe 25 (1007 CE) as Zhongjing Dadingfu (中京大定府), the Central Capital of the Liao dynasty.
b_Liao_Dading.etymology_analysis: Auspicious Chinese capital-prefecture name meaning 'Great Pacification / Great Settlement' (大定), coined by Liao Shengzong in 1007 CE for the Central Capital (Zhongjing).

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE); Jiu Tangshu (945 CE) / Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Zhongjing Dadingfu was built at the former Xi royal encampment where Tang Taizong established the Raole Area Command (饶乐都督府) in 648 CE, on territory earlier attested as Han Xin'anping County (新安平县).

b_Liao_Enzhou.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): '恩州，怀德军，下，刺史。本汉新安平县地。太宗建州。' Established under Liao Taizong (r. 927–947 CE).
b_Liao_Enzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Prefecture of Imperial Grace' (恩州), established by Liao Taizong (r. 927–947 CE) in the Central Capital circuit.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 39) states Enzhou was established on the former territory of Han dynasty Xin'anping County (新安平县).

b_Liao_Songshanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established in the Liao dynasty (c. 10th–11th century) on the grazing lands of Prince Pugu near Mount Song, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37 & 39, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Songshanzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Pine Mountain Prefecture' (松山州), named after Mount Song (松山) in the former pasturelands of the Liaoze tribes.

b_cirlzj_jianting.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Jianting (建亭) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name in the Liao Zhongjing region.
b_cirlzj_jianting.etymology_analysis: Chinese compound meaning 'Established Post/Pavilion' (建亭); no pre-867 historical settlement of this name is attested in the Liao Zhongjing/Chengde area.

b_Liao_Fengzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as a Liao touxia prefecture (c. 10th–11th century) on the grazing lands of Yaonian Sengyin north of Shangjing, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Fengzhou.etymology_analysis: Auspicious Chinese administrative name meaning 'Abundant Prefecture' (丰州), established in the Liao dynasty on Yaolian Khitan pasturelands south of Shangjing (distinct from West Capital Fengzhou in Hohhot).

b_Liao_Yikunzhou.first_mention_attestation: Founded in the early 10th century (c. 920 CE) by Empress Yingtian (Shulü Ping) on Khitan Right Great Tribe territory, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Yikunzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Prefecture of Empress's Virtue/Earthly Rites' (仪坤州), founded by Empress Yingtian (Shulü Ping) at her birthplace.

b_cirlzj_caodangzhen.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Caodangzhen (草当镇) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name.
b_cirlzj_caodangzhen.etymology_analysis: Chinese compound meaning 'Grass-Facing Garrison/Town' (草当镇); no historical settlement of this name is attested in written sources.

b_cirlzj_yudaokou.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Yudaokou (御道口) originated in the Qing dynasty as an entrance pass to the imperial Mulan Paddock hunting grounds (established 1681 CE).
b_cirlzj_yudaokou.etymology_analysis: Chinese toponym meaning 'Imperial Road Pass' (御道口), referring to the Qing emperors' route into the Mulan Paddock hunting reserve in Weichang, Hebei.

b_cirlzj_luexiating.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Luexiating (略下亭) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name.
b_cirlzj_luexiating.etymology_analysis: Chinese compound meaning 'Lower Frontier Post' (略下亭); no pre-867 historical settlement of this name is attested.

b_cirlzj_chengde.first_mention_attestation: Named Chengde (承德) in 1733 CE (Yongzheng 11) when the Qing court established Chengde Direct-Controlled Prefecture (承德直隶州), replacing Rehe Ting (est. 1723 CE) after the Mountain Resort was begun in 1703 CE.
b_cirlzj_chengde.etymology_analysis: Qing imperial administrative name meaning 'Receiving/Upholding [Ancestral] Virtue' (承德, from 承受先祖德泽), coined by the Yongzheng Emperor in 1733 CE.

b_cirlzj_xinghua.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): Xinghua County (兴化县) was established in Tonghe 25 (1007 CE) as the seat of Liao Beianzhou (北安州).
b_cirlzj_xinghua.etymology_analysis: Auspicious Chinese administrative name meaning 'Rising Civilization/Prosperity' (兴化), established in 1007 CE as the county seat of Liao Beianzhou.

b_cirlzj_qinglonghe.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation as a settlement <= 867 CE; named after the Qinglong River (青龙河), a left-bank tributary of the Luan River in northeastern Hebei.
b_cirlzj_qinglonghe.etymology_analysis: Chinese hydronym meaning 'Azure Dragon River' (青龙河), a major tributary of the Luan River in northeastern Hebei.

b_cirlzj_liuheting.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Liuheting (六合亭) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name.
b_cirlzj_liuheting.etymology_analysis: Chinese compound meaning 'Six-Directions/Confluence Pavilion' (六合亭); no pre-867 settlement of this name is attested.

b_cirlzj_beian.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): Beianzhou (北安州) was established by Liao Shengzong in Tonghe 25 (1007 CE) with Han households, governed from Xinghua County.
b_cirlzj_beian.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Northern Pacification' (北安, short for 北安州), established by the Liao dynasty in 1007 CE.

b_cirlzj_chaolijiang.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Chaolijiang (朝里江) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name.
b_cirlzj_chaolijiang.etymology_analysis: Synthetic or unattested Chinese compound meaning 'Court-Village River' (朝里江); no historical settlement or river of this name is attested <= 867 CE.

b_cirlzj_xuefang.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Xuefang (薛坊) is an unattested or synthetic mod barony name.
b_cirlzj_xuefang.etymology_analysis: Chinese compound meaning 'Xue Ward' (薛坊); no pre-867 historical settlement of this name is attested in the Chengde region.

b_Liao_Wuanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): originally built by Liao Taizu as Xingguo Xincheng (later Xinzhou), and renamed Wuanzhou (武安州) in Tonghe 8 (990 CE).
b_Liao_Wuanzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Martial Pacification Prefecture' (武安州), adopted in 990 CE under Liao Shengzong.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945 CE) / Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 39) states Wuanzhou was built on the former territory of Tang dynasty Wozhou (沃州), a jimi prefecture for Khitan/Xi groups restored in Kaiyuan 2 (714 CE).

b_Liao_Jianzhou.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): '建州，保静军，上，节度。唐武德中，置昌乐县。太祖完葺故垒，置州。' Established as Jianzhou under Liao Taizu (r. 907–926 CE).
b_Liao_Jianzhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'Established Prefecture' (建州), founded by Liao Taizu (r. 907–926 CE) by repairing an older Tang-era fortress.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945 CE) / Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 39) records that Tang established Changle County (昌乐县) here during the Wude era (618–626 CE) before Liao Taizu repaired the old fortress to establish Jianzhou.

b_Liao_Gaozhou.first_mention_attestation: Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE): '高州，观察。唐信州之地... 开泰中，圣宗伐高丽，以俘户置高州。' Established during the Kaitai era (1012–1021 CE).
b_Liao_Gaozhou.etymology_analysis: Chinese administrative name meaning 'High Prefecture' (高州), established by Liao Shengzong in the Kaitai era (1012–1021 CE) with captives from Goryeo.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945 CE) / Liao Shi (juan 39, 1344 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: Liao Shi (juan 39) states Gaozhou occupied the former territory of Tang dynasty Xinzhou (信州), established in Wansui Tongtian 1 (696 CE) for the Khitan Shihuo tribe.

b_Amur_Mergen.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; Mergen (墨尔根 / 篾儿干) became a Qing military garrison and served as the provincial capital of Heilongjiang in 1690–1699 CE.

b_fic_eman_konnovanda.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 qualifier compound 黑完达 (Hēiwándá, 'Black Wanda'), calqued into Tarrisch as SwartzVollRêk.

b_fic_eman_hulavanda.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_fic_* CK3 barony name.
b_fic_eman_hulavanda.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 qualifier compound 红完达 (Hóngwándá, 'Red Wanda'), calqued into Tarrisch as RôtVollRêk.

b_Liao_Chaoyang.first_mention_attestation: Named Chaoyang (朝阳) in 1778 CE (Qing Qianlong 43rd year) after Fenghuang Mountain and a Shijing poem; no written attestation of the name Chaoyang <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Chaoyang.etymology_analysis: Qing-era name 朝阳 (Cháoyáng, 'Facing the Morning Sun'), inspired by the Shijing verse on Fenghuang Mountain; calqued into Tarrisch as HôfSunnen.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Attested as Liucheng (柳城) in the Hanshu (111 CE), Longcheng (龙城) as the Three Yan capital in the 4th century, and Yingzhou (营州) under Northern Wei, Sui, and Tang.

b_Liao_Chuanzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Chuanzhou (川州) in 951 CE (Liao Yingli 1st year, renamed from Baichuanzhou), recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Chuanzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 川州 (Chuānzhōu, 'Stream Prefecture', shortened from Baichuanzhou), calqued into Tarrisch as Bachegouwe.

b_Liao_Qianzhou2.first_mention_attestation: Established as Qianzhou (迁州) in 1030 CE (Liao Taiping 10th year) near Shanhaiguan, recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Qianzhou2.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 迁州 (Qiānzhōu, 'Relocation Prefecture'), named for resettled Guizhou households, calqued into Tarrisch as Wandelgouwe.

b_Liao_Chengzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established in 1021 CE (Liao Taiping 1st year) as Muzhou and later renamed Chengzhou (成州), recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Chengzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty princess's touxia prefecture 成州 (Chéngzhōu, 'Accomplished Prefecture') near Fuxin, calqued into Tarrisch as Vollbrâchtgouwe.

b_Liao_Yizhou3.first_mention_attestation: Established as Chongyijun in 990 CE (Liao Tonghe 8th year) and formally as Yizhou (宜州) under Liao Xingzong (1031-1055 CE), recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation of Yizhou <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Yizhou3.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 宜州 (Yízhōu, 'Fitting Prefecture', modern Yi County, Jinzhou), calqued into Tarrisch as Rechtgouwe.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Attested as Jiaoli County (交黎县) in Western Han (Hanshu, 111 CE) and renamed Changli County (昌黎县) in Eastern Han.

b_Liao_Xizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established under Liao Shengzong (r. 982-1031 CE) at Haibin County (southwest of Xingcheng, Liaoning) and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Xizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 隰州 (Xízhōu, 'Lowland Marsh Prefecture'), calqued into Tarrisch as Sompgouwe.

b_Liao_Jinzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Jinzhou (锦州) by Liao Taizu (r. 916-926 CE) and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation of Jinzhou <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Jinzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 锦州 (Jǐnzhōu, 'Brocade Prefecture'), calqued into Tarrisch as Sîdenziergouwe.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Originally Tuhe County (徒河县) in Liaoxi Commandery under Yan and Han, attested in the Hanshu (111 CE).

b_Liao_Liaozhou.first_mention_attestation: Established as Dongpingjun / Liaozhou (辽州) in 924 CE (Liao Tianzan 3rd year) at Liaobin (modern Xinmin, Liaoning), recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Liaozhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 辽州 (Liáozhōu, 'Liao Prefecture') at Liaobin (Xinmin, Liaoning), calqued into Tarrisch as Ljôgouwe.

b_Liao_Suizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established during the Liao dynasty (c. 10th–11th century) at Shanhe northwest of Zhangwu, as recorded in Liao Shi (juan 37, 1344 CE).
b_Liao_Suizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty touxia prefecture 遂州 (Suìzhōu, 'Fulfillment Prefecture'), calqued into Tarrisch as Vollbrengegouwe.

b_Liao_Shuangzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Liao Taizong (r. 927-947 CE) at Shuangcheng (west of modern Tieling, Liaoning) and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Shuangzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 双州 (Shuāngzhōu, 'Twin Prefecture'), named for resettled populations from Zhen and Ding prefectures, calqued into Tarrisch as Twêgouwe.

b_Liao_Xianzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established under Liao Shizong (r. 947-951 CE) at Fengxian County (modern Beizhen, Liaoning) and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation of Xianzhou <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Xianzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 显州 (Xiǎnzhōu, 'Illustrious Prefecture') guarding the Xianling imperial mausoleum, calqued into Tarrisch as Vermaertgouwe.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Attested as Wulu County (无虑县) in the Hanshu (111 CE) and Tang-era Wulu Shouzhoucheng (巫闾守捉城).

b_Liao_Haibeizhou.first_mention_attestation: Established by Liao Shizong (r. 947-951 CE) near modern Yi County, Liaoning, and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Haibeizhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 海北州 (Hǎiběizhōu, 'North-of-the-Sea Prefecture'), calqued into Tarrisch as MêrNordgouwe.

b_Liao_Qianzhou.first_mention_attestation: Established in 985 CE (Liao Tonghe 3rd year) southwest of modern Beizhen, Liaoning, and recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Qianzhou.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 乾州 (Qiánzhōu, 'Heavenly Prefecture') in Beizhen, calqued into Tarrisch as Hêmelgouwe.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Situated in the territory of Han-era Wulu County (无虑县), attested in the Hanshu (111 CE).

b_cirlzj_qinhuangdao.first_mention_attestation: Earliest confirmed written attestation as Qinhuangdao (秦皇岛) in the 1535 CE Ming-era Shanhaiguan Zhi (山海关志); no written attestation of this name <= 867 CE.
b_cirlzj_qinhuangdao.etymology_analysis: Ming-era toponym 秦皇岛 (Qínhuángdǎo, 'Island of the Qin Emperor'), named after Qin Shi Huang's 215 BCE eastern tour; calqued into Tarrisch as ZînKeiserinsel.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Hanshu (Book of Han, 111 CE) Geographical Treatise
older_name_by_867.notes: Western Han Linyu County (临渝县) in Liaoxi Commandery and the coastal landmark Jieshi (碣石) occupied the Qinhuangdao area prior to 867 CE.

b_pingzhou.first_mention_attestation: Attested in the Sanguozhi (Records of the Three Kingdoms, c. 280-289 CE) and Jin Shu (648 CE), following Cao Cao's construction of Pingzhou City (平州城) at Lulong in 207 CE and formal establishment of Pingzhou in 276 CE.
b_pingzhou.etymology_analysis: Historical Chinese province and prefecture 平州 (Píngzhōu, 'Pacified/Level Prefecture') centered at Lulong, Hebei; calqued into Tarrisch as Ebenegouwe.

b_cirlzj_longtan.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; generic/synthetic landscape barony name ('Dragon Pool') in Liaoxi.
b_cirlzj_longtan.etymology_analysis: Generic Chinese landscape name 龙潭 (Lóngtán, 'Dragon Pool'), calqued into Tarrisch as Drachendêpe.

b_cirlzj_yuhejing.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic barony name ('Jade River Well') in Liaoxibei.
b_cirlzj_yuhejing.etymology_analysis: Synthetic Chinese toponym 玉河井 (Yùhéjǐng, 'Jade River Well'), calqued into Tarrisch as Jâdeflôzbrunn.

b_Liao_Liping.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; no historical settlement named Liping (黎平) is attested in Liaoxibei (Guizhou's Liping was a later Ming prefecture).
b_Liao_Liping.etymology_analysis: Chinese toponym 黎平 (Lípíng, 'Li Plain'), calqued into Tarrisch as LîEbene.

b_cirlzj_fusu.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE as a settlement in Liaoxibei; synthetic barony name referencing Qin prince Fusu.
b_cirlzj_fusu.etymology_analysis: Synthetic barony name 扶苏 (Fúsū), referencing Qin prince Fusu (d. 210 BCE), calqued into Tarrisch as StütteSûz.

b_Liao_Andefu.first_mention_attestation: Established as Ande County (安德县) in 990 CE (Liao Tonghe 8th year) and elevated to Andezhou (安德州) in 1043 CE, recorded in Liao Shi (1344 CE); no written attestation <= 867 CE.
b_Liao_Andefu.etymology_analysis: Liao-dynasty prefecture 安德府/安德州 (Āndéfǔ, 'Prefecture of Peaceful Virtue') south of Chaoyang, calqued into Tarrisch as FridDôgetambet.

b_cirlxj_huanzhou.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name (historical Huanzhou was a later Jin-dynasty prefecture).
b_cirlxj_huanzhou.etymology_analysis: CK3 barony 桓州 (Huánzhōu, 'Pillar Prefecture'), calqued into Tarrisch as Stamgouwe.

b_cirlxj_dongting.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name.
b_cirlxj_dongting.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 directional name 东亭 (Dōngtíng, 'East Pavilion'), calqued into Tarrisch as Ôsttorn.

b_cirlxj_nanpo.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name.
b_cirlxj_nanpo.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 directional landscape name 南坡 (Nánpō, 'South Slope'), calqued into Tarrisch as Sûtlîte.

b_cirlxj_yangcheng.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name.
b_cirlxj_yangcheng.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 name 阳城 (Yángchéng, 'Sunny Walled City'), calqued into Tarrisch as Sunnenburch.

b_cirlxj_yunyudi.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name.
b_cirlxj_yunyudi.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 landscape name 云雨地 (Yúnyǔdì, 'Cloud-and-Rain Land'), calqued into Tarrisch as WolchenRêgenlant.

b_cirlxj_lilingtaiyi.first_mention_attestation: No written attestation <= 867 CE; synthetic b_cirlxj_* CK3 barony name.
b_cirlxj_lilingtaiyi.etymology_analysis: Synthetic CK3 name 醴陵台邑 (Lǐlíngtáiyì, 'Sweet-Spring Mound Terrace Town'), calqued into Tarrisch as Sûzewînhügiltornstat.
